nodes.name: FeCoNi-LDH-NWAs
aliases: ternary Fe, Co, Ni-based layered double hydroxide nanowire arrays

nodes.name: Hydrolysis route for FeCoNi-LDH-NWAs
nodes.procedure: 121.2 mg Fe(NO₃)₃·9H₂O, 436.5 mg Co(NO₃)₂·6H₂O, 450 mg (NH₂)₂CO, and 222 mg NH₄F were dissolved into 40 ml ultrapure water and moved into a 45 ml teflon-lined autoclave with steel shell. A piece of Ni foam (1×3 cm, thickness: 1.5 mm, bulk density: 0.3 g/cm³) was cleaned ultrasonically first with ethanol (20 ml), then with 3 M HCl aqueous solution (20 ml) for 15 min, and washed subsequently with deionized water for three times. The as-prepared Ni foam above was immersed into the above autoclave and exactly stuck at the center of the autoclave vertically. The autoclave was sealed and then heated at 120°C for 10 h. The obtained electrode was cleaned with ethanol three times and dried in vacuum at room temperature for further characterizations and next step reaction.

nodes.name: Kirkendall cavitation for FeCoNi-HNTAs
nodes.procedure: First, 15 mg of (NH₄)₂MoS₄ were dissolved in 38 ml of N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) and stirred for 10 min to make solution homogeneous. Then 2 ml HZH (volume fraction, 85%) was introduced dropwise into the foregoing solution with vigorously stirring. The mixed solution for growing hybrid nanotubes was transferred into a 45 ml teflon-lined autoclave with steel shell and FeCoNi-LDH-NWAs was submerged into the above solution and exactly stuck at the direction of autoclave diameter vertically. The autoclave was sealed and then heated at 200°C for 10 h. When the system was cooled down, this obtained electrode was cleaned with ethanol three times and dried in vacuum at room temperature for further characterizations.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show nanowire morphology of FeCoNi-LDH-NWAs (~150 nm diameter) and irregular nanotube array morphology of FeCoNi-HNTAs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Field-emission scanning electron microscope (FESEM) images (Fig. 2a) show the nanowire morphology bound to the substrate along with different directions and uniform diameter size of approximately 150 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD pattern confirms crystalline nature of FeCoNi-HNTAs with characteristic reflections of 1T' MoS2 and (Co,Fe,Ni)9S8 phases.
nodes.evidence_snippet: integrating high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) image (Fig. 2e) and corresponding XRD pattern (Supplementary Fig. 9), the characteristic lattice fringes of (101) planes in MoS2 with inter-planar distances of 0.27 nm were exhibited as well as (222) planes of (Co,Fe,Ni)9S8 with interplanar spacing of 0.29 nm

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping confirms uniform distribution of Fe, Co, Ni, Mo, S, O, N in FeCoNi-HNTAs with ratios Fe:Co:Ni ≈ 1:5:3 and Mo ≈ 11.9 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: We also performed the energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) elemental mapping measurement and found the uniform distribution of the five elements (Supplementary Fig. 3), which further indicated the successful synthesis of trimetal LDH nanowires.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals hollow nature and uneven tube wall of FeCoNi-HNTAs nanotubes with diameter ~150 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: When focusing on a single nanotube in FeCoNi-HNTAs (Fig. 2b, c, d), the diameter size is around 150 nm and the thickness of the tube wall ranges from approximately 30 to 80 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice fringes with spacing of 0.27 nm and 0.29 nm corresponding to (101) planes of MoS2 and (222) planes of (Co,Fe,Ni)9S8.
nodes.evidence_snippet: integrating high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) image (Fig. 2e) ... the characteristic lattice fringes of (101) planes in MoS2 with inter-planar distances of 0.27 nm were exhibited as well as (222) planes of (Co,Fe,Ni)9S8 with interplanar spacing of 0.29 nm

nodes.characterization_summary: AC-STEM images confirm presence of 1T' MoS2 with tetragonal symmetry Mo clusters and cubic symmetry of (Co,Fe,Ni)9S8 crystals.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Typical atomic resolution aberration-corrected scanning TEM (AC-STEM) images clarify the presence of 1T' MoS2 and (Co,Fe,Ni)9S8, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: EXAFS at Mo K-edge shows Mo-Mo bond length of 2.79 Å (vs 3.16 Å in 2H MoS2), confirming metallic 1T' MoS2 phase stability in FeCoNi-HNTAs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The FT profile comparison of EXAFS data at Mo K-edge in R-space (Fig. 3b) exhibits distinct downshift of Mo-Mo bond peak in FeCoNi-HNTAs, demonstrating decreasing bond length from 3.16 to 2.79 Å (Supplementary Table 1), which corresponds to the characteristic peak of Mo–Mo bond in 1T' MoS2.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms major 1T' MoS2 phase (Mo 3d peaks at 228, 231.2 eV) and mixed valence states in FeCoNi-HNTAs: Fe2+/Fe3+ (706.7/710.4/712.8 eV), Co2+/Co3+ (778.0/780.7/782.1 eV), Ni2+/Ni3+ (855.0/856.1 eV).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) spectrum (Fig. 3c) of Mo 3d and S 2s regions of MoS2 in FeCoNi-HNTAs shows the fitting curve from characteristic peaks of 1T' (228 and 231.2 eV) and 2H phase (229 and 232 eV), resulting in the major proportion of 1T' MoS2 in FeCoNi-HNTAs.

nodes.characterization_summary: sXAS at Fe, Co, Ni L3 edges shows increased Fe3+, Co3+ at octahedral sites, and Ni3+ due to synergistic interactions among Fe, Co, Ni ions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: sXAS is performed for direct detection of the 3d valence states of the metals via dipole selection rules.

nodes.characterization_summary: Bubble contact angle measurement shows 171.0° ± 3.4° on FeCoNi-HNTAs surface under electrolyte, confirming superaerophobicity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the bubble contact angle reaches 171.0° ± 3.4° on the surface of FeCoNi-HNTAs under electrolyte (inset 4 in Fig. 4a), indicating the remarkable superaerophobicity of FeCoNi-HNTAs.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ EXAFS at Mo K-edge during HER/OER shows unchanged Mo-Mo bond positions, confirming 1T' MoS2 phase stability under operating potentials.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The in situ XANES spectra from EXAFS (Fig. 7a, c) and corresponding FT profiles (Fig. 7b, d) in R-space of FeCoNi-HNTAs at as-prepared and ongoing electrocatalytic states... the positions of Mo-Mo bond peaks for 1T' MoS2 are unchanged during the applied HER and OER processes
